name: Nord Stream 1 & 2
status: Sabotaged Sep 2022. Nord Stream 1 was operational 2011-2022. NS2 never entered commercial service.
controller: Russia to Germany (destroyed)

name: TurkStream
status: Operational since Jan 2020. Two lines, one supplying Turkey, one transiting to SE Europe.
controller: Russia to Turkey

name: Trans-Anatolian Pipeline (TANAP)
status: Operational since June 2018. Carries Shah Deniz II gas across Turkey.
controller: Azerbaijan to Turkey (connects to TAP at Greek border)

name: Trans-Adriatic Pipeline (TAP)
status: Operational since Dec 2020. Southern Gas Corridor final leg.
operator: TAP AG (BP 20%, SOCAR 20%, Snam 20%, Fluxys 19%, Enagas 16%, Axpo 5%)
controller: Greece to Albania to Italy

name: Blue Stream
status: Operational since 2005. Deepest subsea pipeline in the world at time of construction (2150m).
controller: Russia to Turkey

name: EastMed Pipeline
status: Stalled. Proposed 2018, US withdrew support Jan 2022. Technically challenging deepwater route. Replaced by Egypt LNG focus.
controller: Israel / Cyprus / Greece to Italy (proposed)

name: Power of Siberia
status: Operational since Dec 2019. Ramping up to full capacity by 2025.
controller: Russia to China (Chayandinskoye field to Blagoveshchensk crossing)

name: Power of Siberia 2
status: Under negotiation. Route through Mongolia agreed in principle. No final investment decision as of 2026.
controller: Russia to Mongolia to China (proposed)

name: Central Asia-China Gas Pipeline
status: Operational since 2009. Lines A, B, C active. Line D (Tajikistan route) under construction.
controller: Turkmenistan to Uzbekistan to Kazakhstan to China
capacity: 55 bcm/year (Lines A-C); Line D adds 30 bcm

name: TAPI Pipeline
status: Stalled. Afghan section incomplete due to security. Construction started in Turkmen section 2015.
controller: Turkmenistan to Afghanistan to Pakistan to India (proposed)

name: Iran-Pakistan Pipeline (Peace Pipeline / IP)
status: Partially built. Iran section (900km) complete. Pakistan section stalled under US sanctions pressure.
controller: Iran to Pakistan (India withdrew 2009)

name: Arab Gas Pipeline
status: Limited operation. Egyptian section active; Syrian section damaged in civil war. Jordan receives intermittent supply.
controller: Egypt to Jordan to Syria to Lebanon

name: Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline (TSGP / NIGAL)
status: Planned. MoU signed Nigeria-Niger-Algeria 2022. Construction not started. 4,128km proposed route.
controller: Nigeria to Niger to Algeria to Europe (planned)

name: South Caucasus Pipeline (Baku-Tbilisi-Erzurum / SCP)
status: Operational since 2006. Expanded (SCPX) 2018 for Shah Deniz II. Feeds into TANAP.
controller: Azerbaijan to Georgia to Turkey

name: Yamal-Europe Pipeline
status: Reduced flow. Poland seized Gazprom's stake in EuRoPol Gaz (Nov 2022). Reverse flows active. Russia cut supply May 2022.
operator: Gazprom (Russia section) / EuRoPol Gaz (Poland section) / GASCADE (Germany section)
controller: Russia to Belarus to Poland to Germany

name: BTC Pipeline (Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan)
status: Operational since 2006. Key non-Russian export route for Caspian crude. Carries ~1% of global oil supply.
operator: BP (30.1%), SOCAR (25%), others in BTC Co.
controller: Azerbaijan to Georgia to Turkey

name: Druzhba Pipeline (Friendship Pipeline)
status: Partially operational under EU sanctions. Northern leg (to Germany/Poland) halted. Southern leg (to Hungary/Czechia/Slovakia) still flowing via exemption.
controller: Russia to Central Europe (split into northern and southern branches at Mozyr, Belarus)

name: Druzhba Pipeline (Southern Branch)
status: Operational under EU sanctions exemption. Supplies landlocked Hungary, Slovakia, and Czech Republic.
controller: Russia to Ukraine to Slovakia/Hungary/Czech Republic

name: CPC Pipeline (Caspian Pipeline Consortium)
status: Operational since 2001. Expanded 2015. Key Kazakh crude export route. Russia occasionally disrupts citing 'maintenance'.
controller: Kazakhstan to Russia Black Sea coast (Novorossiysk)

name: Kirkuk-Ceyhan Pipeline
status: Intermittent. Shut down March 2023 after international arbitration ruling. Turkey and Iraq negotiating restart. Sabotaged repeatedly during insurgency.
controller: Iraq (KRG/federal dispute) to Turkey

name: ESPO Pipeline (Eastern Siberia-Pacific Ocean)
status: Operational. ESPO-1 since 2009, ESPO-2 since 2012. Major route for Russian crude to China and Asia-Pacific post-sanctions.
controller: Russia (Taishet to Kozmino Bay), with spur to China at Skovorodino

name: ESPO-China Spur (Skovorodino-Mohe)
status: Operational since 2011. Doubled capacity 2018. Russia's primary crude delivery route to China.
controller: Russia to China

name: Keystone Pipeline System
status: Keystone original operational since 2010. Keystone XL permit revoked by Biden Jan 2021, cancelled by TC Energy. Keystone mainline spill Dec 2022 in Kansas.
controller: Canada (Alberta) to United States (Gulf Coast refineries)
capacity: 590,000 barrels/day (original Keystone); XL would have added 830,000 bpd

name: Trans-Alaska Pipeline System (TAPS)
status: Operational since 1977. Flow declining from peak 2.1 mbpd (1988) to ~0.5 mbpd. 800 miles across Alaska.
operator: Alyeska Pipeline Service Company (BP, ConocoPhillips, ExxonMobil consortium)
controller: United States (Prudhoe Bay to Valdez marine terminal)

name: SUMED Pipeline (Suez-Mediterranean)
status: Operational since 1977. Bypasses Suez Canal for supertankers too large for the canal. Critical chokepoint alternative.
controller: Egypt

name: Trans-Arabian Pipeline (Tapline)
status: Decommissioned. Operational 1950-1976. Once the world's largest oil pipeline. Shut down due to transit fee disputes and regional instability.
controller: Saudi Arabia to Lebanon (decommissioned)

name: East-West Pipeline (Petroline)
status: Operational since 1981. Key Saudi strategic pipeline allowing oil exports to bypass Strait of Hormuz via Red Sea.
controller: Saudi Arabia (Abqaiq to Yanbu on Red Sea coast)
